[](https://www.theverge.com/tech/918857/the-long-rumored-foldable-ipad-may-never-see-the-light-of-day)

![Image 4: Terrence O'Brien](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/TERRENCE_BLURPLE.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=96)

Terrence O'Brien Apr 26

The long rumored foldable iPad may never see the light of day.

Apple has supposedly been working on a folding tablet since at least 2023. The rumored release has slipped from [2024](https://www.theverge.com/2023/1/30/23577407/apple-ipad-foldable-analyst-ming-chi-kuo-2024-release-date), to [2026](https://www.theverge.com/2024/2/2/24059002/foldable-ipad-in-2026), to [2028](https://www.theverge.com/2024/12/15/24321659/apple-foldable-18-8-inch-ipad-invisible-crease-rumor), to [2029](https://www.theverge.com/news/803899/apples-rumored-foldable-18-inch-ipad-is-delayed-until-2029-due-to-engineering-challenges), and now, [according to Mark Gurman](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-04-26/new-apple-ceo-john-ternus-first-major-product-is-the-foldable-iphone-road-map-mofu521p), it might not happen at all. While it was a priority for incoming CEO John Ternus, its future is now in doubt:

> Foldable iPad: Apple has been working on a roughly 20-inch foldable iPad. This device has been a Ternus priority but may end up being a wacky experiment that doesn’t see the light of day, according to several people who have worked on it.

There’s the way any good noir is meant to be consumed — in [high-contrast monochrome](https://youtu.be/DfowFyDxUXo) below. And then there is a “[True-Hue Full Color](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LpN2RavI5C8)” that frankly sucks all the fun out of it and just serves to highlight the seams in the mediocre CGI.

![Image 10: Terrence O'Brien](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/TERRENCE_BLURPLE.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=96)

Terrence O'Brien Apr 26

New Art City is a free virtual gallery filled with beautifully bizarre art.

There are dozens of exhibitions that you can walk through in your browser. Some feature [3D scanned sculptures](https://newart.city/show/blobtopia-brainrotting-wasteland), others are [glitchy worlds](https://newart.city/show/pure-land-2022) populated by sound experiments, and some have [branching poetry](https://newart.city/show/earth-stepper-hell-kettle-mere) for you to explore. Each 3D world is “multiplayer”, so you can visit a virtual opening and chat with other art fans.

[New Art City: Virtual Art Space](https://newart.city/)
[New Art City • Virtual Art Space]

![Image 13: Terrence O'Brien](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/TERRENCE_BLURPLE.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=96)

Terrence O'Brien Apr 25

ADT confirms customer data was stolen in a breach.

The [prolific](https://www.theverge.com/2024/5/31/24169112/ticketmaster-data-breach-confirmed-details-live-nation)[ShinyHunters](https://www.theverge.com/games/910815/rockstar-games-says-hack-will-have-no-impact)[group](https://www.theverge.com/tech/914723/vercel-hacked) is [claiming responsibility](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/adt-confirms-data-breach-after-shinyhunters-leak-threat/) and threatening to leak the stolen data unless a ransom is paid. [ADT has said](https://newsroom.adt.com/corporate-news/adt-detects-cybersecurity-incident) that the info was mostly limited to names, phone numbers, and addresses, and that credit card or bank account information was not compromised.

> The investigation confirmed that the information involved was limited to names, phone numbers, and addresses. In a small percentage of cases, dates of birth and the last four digits of Social Security numbers or Tax IDs were included. Critically, no payment information — including bank accounts or credit cards — was accessed, and customer security systems were not affected or compromised in any way.

[ADT detects cybersecurity incident](https://newsroom.adt.com/corporate-news/adt-detects-cybersecurity-incident)

Stream your slop while you drive.

Suno is available on Android Auto, and CarPlay support is in the works. Now you can stream all your [illicit AI covers](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/906896/sunos-copyright-ai-music-covers) on your road trip from Hell. According to a [post](https://discord.com/channels/1069381916492562582/1083140371980234852/1497318765556142202) in the Suno Discord, features are limited, with only search, library and explore support, plus playback control.

Spotify is finally bringing playlist folders to its mobile apps.

Organizing playlists into folders was introduced in 2010, but only available on the desktop app. Now it’s reportedly [rolling out to mobile users](https://www.androidauthority.com/spotify-playlist-folders-mobile-rollout-3660742/). Tap the + icon in your library, and you [should see](https://www.reddit.com/r/truespotify/comments/1sty6ct/you_can_now_create_folders_on_mobile_and_move/) a new “folder” option. You can even play an entire folder of playlists, or shuffle them.

Norway could be the next nation to ban kids from social media.

As [_Reuters_](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/norway-government-plans-social-media-ban-children-under-16-2026-04-24/) reports, Norwegian Prime ​Minister Jonas Gahr Støre [announced plans](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/whats-new/norwegian-social-media-age-restrictions-law-on-track-to-be-introduced-this-year-this-is-how-the-age-limit-for-social-media-will-work/id3157276/) for a bill barring teens from social media until “January 1st the year a child turns 16,” similar to [Australia’s](https://www.theverge.com/report/840822/australia-social-media-ban-under-16-response).

> “I can now confirm that we are planning to submit a bill to the Parliament before the end of the year. We are introducing this legislation because we want a childhood where children get to be children. Play, friendships, and everyday life must not be taken over by algorithms and screens.”

Tom Warren Apr 24

GitHub just had a major outage.

GitHub uses a queue for developers when lots of people are working on a single project. It’s designed to avoid changes clashing and developers breaking things, but [yesterday it failed](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/zsg1lk7w13cf) in a catastrophic way [thanks to a bug](https://x.com/akshat_b/status/2047501765138928050?s=46) that randomly reverted previously merged commits (code snapshots). GitHub also had [other outages](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/myrbk7jvvs6p) yesterday, on the same day I reported on employee concerns about GitHub reliability and leadership.
